# Section 010: Compute Placement And Sizing

The reader gives one workload the CPU and memory it needs and puts its pods on the right nodes. Requests and limits come first because every later section builds on them: the scheduler places by requests, the HPA scales on utilisation of requests, OpenCost allocates by requests, and quotas count them.

**Curriculum item covered:** Applying Platform Architecture Best Practices for Networking, Storage, and Compute

---

## What You Will Master

- Set CPU and memory requests and limits on a container and read them back with kubectl get -o yaml
- Predict the QoS class (Guaranteed, Burstable, BestEffort) of a pod from its resources and confirm it in status.qosClass
- Diagnose a Pending pod whose requests do not fit any node from its FailedScheduling event
- Distinguish a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (OOMKilled) from a CPU-throttled container
- Compare a node's allocatable capacity with the sum of requests using kubectl describe node
- Locate the resources fields in the Kubernetes API reference and the resource management documentation
- Pin pods to labelled nodes with required node affinity and prefer nodes with preferred node affinity
- Reserve a node for one workload with a NoSchedule taint and a matching toleration
- Explain from pod events why a toleration alone does not move a pod onto a tainted node
- Keep replicas apart with pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname
- Spread replicas evenly across zones with a topology spread constraint and read the effect of maxSkew and whenUnsatisfiable
- Diagnose a Pending pod caused by an unmatched affinity rule or an untolerated taint from its FailedScheduling message

## The Learning Path

### 1. Set Requests, Limits And QoS Classes
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Set Requests, Limits And QoS Classes](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-010/module-01/playground` — Single-node kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.35) with metrics-server (--kubelet-insecure-tls). Namespace `starfleet` with `scout` (podinfo) in three variants: `scout-guaranteed` (requests equal limits), `scout-burstable` (requests below limits) and `scout-besteffort` (no resources), plus `shuttle`. A manifest for a `scout-oversized` Deployment whose memory request exceeds the node's allocatable is ready to apply, so the reader can see a Pending pod. podinfo's stress endpoints are reachable from `shuttle` to show CPU throttling and an OOMKilled restart. No LimitRange or ResourceQuota.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-010/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Place Workloads With Affinity, Taints And Topology Spread
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Place Workloads With Affinity, Taints And Topology Spread](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-010/module-02/playground` — Three-node kind cluster (one control plane, two workers; note the extra memory cost). Workers labelled topology.kubernetes.io/zone=zone-a and zone-b, and one worker labelled `disktype=ssd`. The zone-b worker carries the taint `dedicated=outpost:NoSchedule`. Namespace `starfleet` with `scout` (3 replicas, no placement rules, so the reader sees uneven placement) and `shuttle`. Namespace `outpost` with `probe` without a toleration. No PriorityClasses.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-010/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Compute Placement And Sizing Capstone — `sections/section-010/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-010/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** A three-node cluster runs `scout` with no resources set, all replicas on one worker, and a `probe` in `outpost` stuck Pending on a tainted node. The reader sets requests and limits that give `scout` the Guaranteed QoS class, spreads its replicas across both zones, and dedicates the tainted worker to `outpost` with a toleration plus node affinity, proving each with pod placement and status.qosClass.
